title: Latency-Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt-5-mini
abstract: We preregistered (CAND-2026-001) and executed an artifact-backed paired experiment that measures whether inserting a selective low-latency verification tier (risk scoring + fast validator) into a generate–validate–repair NetOps pipeline reduces unsafe commits from LLM-generated configuration proposals while satisfying an operational latency SLO. Using a deterministic synthetic intent corpus of 400 paired operator intents (10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a deterministic full-checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) as ground truth, we observed: baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975), guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Model-call accounting reflects the preregistered shared-initial design: planned budget enumerated 800 model generations but observed model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial generations + 1 repair). The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2: 95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms) could not be evaluated because end-to-end latency telemetry was not recorded in the archived confirmatory artifacts; we disclose that absence and provide full provenance for all archived raw outputs, validator traces, per-episode scorer JSONs, and provider-call logs (SHA‑256 cataloged in the execution manifest). We discuss ceiling effects, the shared-initial estimand, representative failure diagnostics, and concrete reproducibility paths for follow-up runs that record latency telemetry and expand model/validator diversity.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation and change workflows promises large operational savings but raises safety concerns when generated configuration proposals are incorrect, violate operational constraints, or introduce regressions. The generate–validate–repair architecture mitigates risk by validating LLM proposals before commit, yet full verification can impose unacceptable latency for time-sensitive operator flows. We preregistered (CAND-2026-001) a paired, confirmatory study that asks: Can a selective, low-latency verification tier (risk scorer + fast verifier) integrated into a generate–validate–repair pipeline reduce unsafe commits relative to LLM-only while meeting a preregistered latency SLO? Contributions: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation comparing guarded selective verification and LLM-only on 400 deterministic NetOps intents; (2) deterministic reconciliation of planned vs observed model-call accounting under a shared-initial design (observed model_calls_used = 401 vs planned 800); (3) public, inspectable evidence traces (per-episode scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider-call logs) enabling reproducible failure-mode inspection and exact reanalysis.
sections.related_work: LLM-driven NetOps and verifier-augmented repair loops have become active research directions. Recent benchmarking and experimental studies evaluate LLM configuration repair, agentic verifier-augmented pipelines, and network-digital-twin validation. Representative prior artifacts (archived alongside this run) include large-scale configuration-repair benchmarks and agentic evaluation studies; our work differs by producing a preregistered paired estimate with exhaustive per-episode provenance and by reconciling shared-initial generation accounting. Key nearest-work references (artifact-backed in the evidence bundle) include Cornetto-style configuration-repair benchmarking (arXiv:2604.22513), agentic configuration-repair evaluations (arXiv:2606.06212), and agentic NetOps with digital-twin validation (arXiv:2604.18233). We position our study as an operationally precise, provenance-rich complement to those works.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and hypotheses
- Preregistration: study CAND-2026-001 was frozen before execution. Primary confirmatory hypotheses: H1 (safety) — guarded selective verification yields a lower unsafe-commit rate than LLM-only (paired); H2 (latency) — guarded pipeline 95th-percentile latency ≤ 2000 ms and lower than full-verification baseline. The preregistration, estimands, sampling plan, retry policy, and analysis scripts (paired_binary_analysis_v1) are archived (preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in execution manifest).
Corpus, tasks, and generators
- Confirmatory corpus: 400 deterministic paired intents generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; 10% (40 intents) are predetermined adversarial/OOD variants as required by the preregistration. Task manifests, reference answers, and intent metadata are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Representative task example: pair-000001 (manifest and responses archived at execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json, SHA-256: ea8359dbe5a5d054...).
Pipeline variants and shared-initial design
- Baseline: accept LLM candidate (LLM-only). Guarded: shared initial candidate generation plus a selective risk-scorer and a fast verifier/repair stage that triggers for flagged candidates before final full-checker validation. To control generator variance, the preregistration allowed a shared-initial candidate per intent reused across both conditions (independent_condition_generation=false). This is the executed design; the preregistration enumerated 800 planned_model_calls under an independent-generation accounting convention but permitted shared-initial operation; observed model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial + 1 repair). The deterministic reconciliation artifact documents this (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).
Validator, scoring, and primary estimand
- Ground-truth functional checker (scorer): deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Per-episode scoring uses full_intent_constraint_validation; scorer outputs per-episode JSONs stored under execution/scoring/*.json. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Primary test: exact McNemar two-sided; CI via paired bootstrap percentile (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Missingness, retry and exclusion rules were followed as preregistered; no unrecovered infrastructure failures occurred.
Reproducibility artifacts and provenance
- All raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per-episode scorer JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), validator traces, provider-call logs (execution/provider_calls/*.json), model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version: gpt-5-mini), and the execution manifest with comprehensive SHA‑256 catalog are archived. Key artifact paths and SHA values are included in the Disclosure Statement below.
sections.results:
Confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed):
- Completed pairs: 400 (complete_pair_count = 400; see analysis/missingness_summary.csv, SHA-256: 9266951e...).
- Baseline valid proposals: 399/400 (0.9975).
- Guarded valid proposals: 400/400 (1.000).
- Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 399, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, SHA-256: a6906bb4...).
- Primary estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Analysis artifacts (condition_summary.csv, paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis_log.jsonl) are archived with SHA‑256 hashes.
Model-call accounting and reconciliation:
- Preregistered planned_model_calls = 800 (enumerated under independent-generation accounting). Executed shared-initial design produced observed model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial + 1 repair). The deterministic reconciliation and provider-call audit are archived (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution manifest). The per-call logs are in execution/provider_calls/ (examples and many SHA‑256 entries in the execution manifest).
Representative discordant episode (artifact mapping):
- The single discordant pair (n10 = 1) can be inspected in the archived per-episode scorer JSONs: execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (SHA‑256: fe147f43...) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (SHA‑256: d0cbfe9a...). Those files contain the baseline candidate, guarded corrected candidate, validator trace, and precise violation codes for replay and forensic inspection. All per-episode scorer JSONs are archived under execution/scoring/.
Latency SLO (H2):
- The preregistered H2 required end-to-end latency telemetry. Those timing traces were not recorded in the confirmatory artifact bundle; H2 is therefore unresolved from this run. The absence of latency telemetry is logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; we explicitly disclose this missingness rather than impute latency.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and operational significance
- The observed absolute safety improvement is small (0.25 percentage points) because the baseline generator+validator pipeline already produced nearly all valid proposals (399/400). With a near-ceiling baseline, the marginal detectability of safety gains is limited; the paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0075] quantifies plausible effect sizes. Practically, selective verification yields minimal additional safety in high-quality generator/validator regimes; benefits are likely larger in lower-baseline or adversarial-rich settings.
Shared-initial design trade-offs
- The preregistered shared-initial candidate design reduces generator variance and focuses the estimand on verifier/repair impact conditional on a fixed candidate. This produces fewer model calls and deterministic pairing but does not measure the joint effect of re-sampling the generator per condition. Both estimands are operationally relevant: shared-initial isolates verifier efficacy; independent-generation captures end-to-end pipeline differences. We document which estimand was executed and provide artifacts (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) enabling secondary analyses.
Representative failure-mode diagnostics
- The lone discordant example demonstrates a baseline candidate that violated a dependency the guarded pipeline corrected. That episode's full traces (baseline and guarded scorer JSONs, validator traces, and provider-call logs) are archived for replay. These artifact-backed example(s) illustrate concrete failure types and how selective verification/repair can intervene.
Reproducibility and archival completeness
- All numerical claims in Results are reproducible from archived artifacts: raw responses, per-episode scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider-call logs, analysis CSVs, and the execution manifest with SHA‑256 for every archived file. The Disclosure Statement below cites the initial master prompt archive (provenance/master_prompt.txt) and its SHA‑256. Analysts can recompute the reported paired table and bootstrap CIs from analysis scripts and artifacts provided.
Implications for operational deployment and follow-up experiments
- Where baseline generation is lower or adversarial exposure higher, selective verification is likely to yield larger safety gains; follow-up preregistered runs should: (1) record end-to-end per-stage latency telemetry to evaluate H2 and latency trade-offs; (2) perform independent-generation (re-sampling) to measure joint generator+verifier effects; (3) sweep selective risk thresholds and adversarial ratios to map the verification-budget vs unsafe-commit Pareto frontier; (4) broaden model and validator diversity to assess external validity. All follow-ups should archive the same per-episode artifacts and SHA‑256 manifests as done here.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a fully preregistered, provenance-rich paired experiment evaluating selective low-latency verification for LLM-driven NetOps pipelines. Under the preregistered synthetic corpus, single model (gpt-5-mini), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and shared-initial candidate design, the guarded intervention produced a numerically small absolute safety gain (0.25 percentage points) over an already-high baseline. The effect is artifact-backed but not statistically distinguishable from zero given the near-ceiling baseline. The preregistered latency SLO (H2) could not be evaluated because the required latency telemetry was not archived; that absence is disclosed. All raw outputs, per-episode scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes and paths in the execution manifest to enable reproducible follow-up runs that record latency and broaden model/validator conditions.

limitations: Synthetic confirmatory corpus and ceiling baseline: the 400-item deterministic intent corpus is synthetic and produced a very high baseline generator+validator success rate (399/400), which limits observable marginal safety gains and reduces statistical power to detect small improvements.

Single-model and single-validator scope: the run used gpt-5-mini as the generator and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Results do not generalize across model families or validators without additional artifact-backed runs.

Shared-initial estimand: the executed shared-initial candidate design isolates verifier/repair impact conditional on a fixed generated candidate; it does not quantify the joint effect of independently re-sampling the generator per condition (independent-generation estimand).

Missing latency telemetry: the preregistered latency hypothesis (H2) required per-stage end-to-end timing traces; these were not archived for the confirmatory run, so latency claims are unresolved and must be tested in a follow-up run that records and archives telemetry.

Digital-twin fidelity: the deterministic validator is a digital-twin style checker; residual uncertainty remains about real-device divergences and environmental effects absent a real-device execution trace.
